harnessTools.askRequesterText: No requester response is available during this evaluation.
harnessTools.conditionElements: a filter condition with elements any holds when at least one value at its field satisfies its comparison, with elements none when no value does; the values are found as a source path finds records (* takes every element of a list, a list at the end gives its elements, an element lacking the rest of the field is left out), so an empty list or a missing field has none; a condition whose field has a * path segment and no elements is refused; any other condition without elements is unchanged
harnessTools.coverageLine: after the read line, when there is something to say, one line "coverage: " of at most coverageLineChars characters: per field that some records lack or hold null, how many have it; what each condition did alone when a filter kept nothing; the records a sum added; a null among distinct values; the size of each set in the order of the sources; groups that are not unique values of one field; and, when a source carries totalCount, total or hasMore or is a shortened calculate output, that the sources hold fewer (or more) records than the total it states, or as many from several pages of which two at one place share no record, none states its place in a list (offset, page, hasMore) or each says hasMore, which stays with every output built from it; the lists the sources read count together when they have the same name, with or without a total and whatever their fields, and a list is short only when all the records of that name are fewer than its total; a record that two pages hold is seen as one only where the plain values that every record has tell the records of each page apart; it never says that a list is complete
harnessTools.readLine: every successful calculate output begins, after its id line, with one line "read: " naming per source, in the order given, the result id, the path, the records it contributed, whether the path matched nothing and how many elements were left out for lacking which step of the path; it never adds the sources up
harnessTools.refusals: refused, with every problem of the call named at once and the shapes of the sources where the problem is one of shape: an argument of the wrong form, named with the form it takes; a key that a source, a condition or an operand does not take; an argument that does not apply to the operation; a field on a source of plain values; a field that no record of any source has, except in a condition that compares it with null; a * in a field outside a filter condition with elements; a * at an object (an XML element that occurs once counts as a list of one); a comparison of a list or an object with one value without elements; conditions that contradict each other; a key with a dot in its name spelled as nested steps (written in brackets, [a.b]); a step in brackets that the objects of one call answer by more than one key; an output longer than maxStoredOutputChars characters
harnessTools.resultIdFormat: <4 hex run tag>-<n>, shown as the first line "result_id: <id>" of every scenario tool result and every successful calculate result
harnessTools.storedResults: a scenario result or a calculate output longer than storeAboveChars characters is stored in full and shown as its id, its size and its shape (lists cut to their first element and their length, objects to previewKeys keys, texts to previewTextChars characters, the whole within previewChars); view reads any part of any result, at most viewPageChars characters a page, with nextOffset for the next page, and a page is always shown in full; shorter results are shown in full; the coverage and warning lines of a calculate output count toward storeAboveChars, and a view page carries its lines above it

tools.description: Compute over results you already obtained in this task; it fetches nothing. Every tool result starts with a line result_id: <id>. A result longer than 5000 characters, a calculate result included, is stored, not shown: you see its size and its shape, where a list shows its first element and its length; read any part of it with view. Every calculate result then has a line read: that names, for each source in turn, its result id, its path, the records it gave and whether the path matched nothing; it does not add the sources up, as they can overlap. Name one or more results in sources, each with an optional path to the part to use, and one generic operation. The records are the elements found at the paths of all sources, one after the other. view: the part at the path of one source; offset and limit page through a list, the keys of an object or the characters of a text; a page holds at most 5000 characters and nextOffset gives the offset of the next page. count: the number of records. distinct: the distinct values of field. group_by: groups by the fields in group_by (an empty list gives one group over all records), with aggregate count or sum of sum_field. sort: the records ordered by field (descending optional). filter: the records for which every condition holds (eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge against a literal value); a condition with elements any holds when at least one value at its field does, with elements none when no value does, where * in the field takes every element of a list and a list at its end gives its elements (an empty list or a missing field has no values); a field with a * segment needs elements any or none. union, intersection, difference: set operations on the values of field taken per source (difference: the first source minus the others). arithmetic: operator add, subtract, multiply or divide over operands, each a number or {result_id, path} naming one number. fields and limit shorten a list of records; round sets decimal places. A field is a dot-separated path inside a record; empty means the record itself. A key with a dot in its name is written in brackets: [a.b]. The result has a result_id of its own. A wrong use is refused with every problem named at once. After read:, a line coverage: names fields that some records lack, the size of each set and records short of totalCount; a line warning: flags repeats, held pages left out and fixed list positions.

path.description: Optional. Dot-separated keys or list positions into that result; * takes every element of a list. A text that holds JSON or XML is read as such. Empty means the whole result.

result_id.description: The id from the first line of an earlier result of this task.
